values.where: Wind Recirculation Zones on Flat-Roofed Buildings
Fundamentals Airflow Around Buildings chapter not found on an official free site

unsupported_wording: Checked against the 2019 I-P text. (1) It says recirculation 'can be an even more serious problem', not 'can be a serious problem'. (2) The equipment is described as units that 'take in air on one side and discharge heated, moist air horizontally from the other side', not intake and exhaust 'on the same housing'. (3) It names Legionnaires' disease, not 'Legionella'. 'Considerably hotter', the reduced capacity of cooling towers and air-cooled condensers, 'can drastically reduce equipment performance', the three recirculation causes, Lr = R and keeping towers away from intakes, operable windows and outdoor public areas are all supported.
note: Not reachable: the SI library edition and the Fundamentals chapter were not reached. Marked false for the cited copy. The 2019 I-P comparison is supporting evidence only. The towers-away-from-intakes advice is credited to ASHRAE Guideline 12.
